title: Unexplored regions of the protein sequence-structure map revealed at scale by a library of foldtuned language models.
authors: Subramanian, Arjuna M; Martinez, Zachary A; Lourenco, Alec L; Yuan, Sonia C; Liu, Shichen; Thomson, Matt
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
one_liner_zh: 该文利用折叠调优的蛋白质语言模型探索远天然序列空间并生成稳定折叠的蛋白变体，虽涉及DNA结合域但非核心TF-DNA互作体系，方法可迁移至TF-DNA结合建模。
abstract: The combinatorial scale of amino-acid sequence-space has traditionally precluded substantive study of the full protein sequence-structure map. It remains unknown, for instance, how much of the vast uncharted landscape of far-from-natural sequences encodes the familiar ensemble of natural folds in a fashion consistent with the laws of biophysics but seemingly untouched by evolution on Earth. The scale of sequence perturbations required to access these spaces exceeds the reach of even gold-standard experimental approaches such as directed evolution. We surpass this limitation guided by the innate capacity of protein language models (PLMs) to explore sequences outside their natural training data through generation and self-feedback. We recast PLMs as probes that explore into regions of protein "deep space" that possess little-to-no detectable homology to natural examples, while enforcing core structural constraints, in a novel sequence design approach that we term "foldtuning." We build a library of foldtuned PLMs for >700 natural folds in the SCOP database, covering numerous high-priority targets for synthetic biology, including GPCRs and small GTPases, composable cell-surface-receptor and DNA-binding domains, and small signaling/regulatory domains. Candidate proteins generated by foldtuned PLMs reflect distinctive new "rules of language" for sequence innovation beyond detectable homology to any known protein and sample subtle structural alterations in a manner reminiscent of natural structural evolution and diversification. Experimental validation of three markedly different fold targets; the tyrosine-kinase- and small-GTPase-regulating SH3 domain, the bacterial RNase inhibitor barstar, and the peptide hormone insulin demonstrates that foldtuning proposes protein variants that express and fold stably in vitro and function in vivo. Foldtuning reveals protein sequence-structure information at scale outside of the context of evolution and promises to push forward the redesign and reconstitution of novel-to-nature synthetic biological systems for applications in health and catalysis.
abstract_zh: 氨基酸序列空间的组合规模传统上阻碍了对完整蛋白质序列-结构图谱的实质性研究。例如，尚不清楚在远离天然序列的广阔未探索景观中，有多少编码了熟悉的天然折叠集合，且符合生物物理学规律，但似乎在地球进化中未被触及。进入这些空间所需的序列扰动规模超出了甚至金标准实验方法（如定向进化）的覆盖范围。我们借助蛋白质语言模型（PLMs）在生成和自反馈过程中探索其天然训练数据之外序列的固有潜力，超越了这一限制。我们将PLMs重新定位为探针，探索与天然实例几乎没有可检测同源性的蛋白质“深空”区域，同时强制执行核心结构约束，这一新型序列设计方法我们称之为“折叠调优 (foldtuning)”。我们为SCOP数据库中超过700种天然折叠构建了折叠调优PLM库，覆盖合成生物学的众多高优先级靶标，包括GPCRs和小GTPases、可组合的细胞表面受体和DNA结合域，以及小信号/调控域。由折叠调优PLMs生成的候选蛋白质反映了序列创新的独特新“语言规则”，超越了与任何已知蛋白质的可检测同源性，并以类似于天然结构进化和多样化的方式采样细微的结构变化。对三个显著不同折叠靶标的实验验证——酪氨酸激酶和小GTPase调控的SH3域、细菌RNase抑制剂barstar，以及肽激素胰岛素——表明折叠调优提出的蛋白质变体在体外表达并稳定折叠，且在体内发挥功能。折叠调优在进化背景之外大规模揭示了蛋白质序列-结构信息，并有望推动新型天然合成生物系统的重新设计和重构，以应用于健康和催化领域。
